chunks: From him, from Mulla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

two witnesses who testified upon one matter, and two others came and testified upon other than which they had testified, and they differed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Lots would be drawn between them, so whoever the lot comes out to for the swearing of the oath, he is the first to be judged for [the claim].'
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence resolve conflicting testimonies from multiple pairs of witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the juristic mechanism of 'qara'' (casting lots) to resolve conflicting testimonies when two pairs of witnesses provide contradictory accounts, a method endorsed by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). It highlights the Shia scholarly approach to judicial uncertainty, where, in the absence of definitive proof, a random selection determines which testimony prevails, ensuring procedural fairness in court rulings. This practice underscores the importance of decisive legal resolution even when evidence is equally weighted but mutually exclusive.

en.hubeali: From him, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Dawood Bin Sirham,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding two witnesses who testified upon one matter and two others came over, so they testified upon other than which they had testified, and they differed. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Lots would be drawn between them, so whoever the lot comes out to for the swearing of the oath, so he would be the first to be judged for’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has narrated the following: “About

the case of two witnesses who testify about one thing and two others testify differently, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that a raffle must be arranged and whoever ’s name comes out to take an oath then judgment must be issued in his favor.’”
